note: Adapted from the species description of Sands (1972); the original is in English and the genus has no soldier caste, only the alate and worker being described; measurement tables, figure numbers, type specimens and distribution records are not translated.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Originally confused with Alyscotermes kilimandjaricus, from which it was later separated by principal component analysis as an outlier from the cluster formed by the numerous specimens of that species, the compound-ratio plots also supporting this separation. Comparisons with A. aganus and A. mitis are given under the former species. A. ignavus and A. murcus are distinguished from this species by the very long head hairs of the alate, projecting from among the shorter felt, the larger fontanelle, the more weakly inflated postclypeus, and in the worker by the very slender fore tibia with a reduced third apical spur. Whether the abdomen dehisces is not known.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule pale yellow, pilosity yellow, very sparse and inconspicuous. Postclypeus strongly inflated, Pcl/W 0.33, Pcl/Ri 3.01; apical tooth of mandibles moderately long, La/Li 0.72, Ra/Ri 1.00; accessory marginal tooth of the left mandible separated from the molar prominence in surface view by a distinct notch, compound ratio 14.41; tip of the first marginal tooth of the right mandible slightly posterior to the line from the apical to the second marginal tooth, compound ratio 18.20. Fore tibia hardly inflated, Ti/Ty 4.73, third apical spur distinct, about one third the size of the other two. Junction of mesenteron and proctodaeum oblique, to the right of the Malpighian nodule; enteric valve seating lateral in the undissected abdomen, distinctly bilobed, connected to the second proctodaeal pouch by a neck of moderate length; membranous wall of the valve with sparse spinules outside the inner cushions.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule chestnut brown, not darkened above the ocelli; fontanelle less than half the length of the ocellus, oval, flat or slightly raised, pale yellowish brown; mid-spot subcircular, flat, as large as the fontanelle, brown; postclypeus brown, labrum yellowish brown; frontal mark distinct, crescent-shaped, slightly depressed, pale brown; antennae yellowish brown. Pronotum brown, meso- and metanotum brown, both with a transverse dark suture, that of the metanotum stronger; femora brown, tibiae yellowish brown, tarsi yellow. Abdominal tergites brown, dorsal spiracles pale brown, sternites pale brown with a pale yellow middle, ventral spiracles pale brown; cerci pale yellow. Posterior margin of head capsule evenly rounded; ocelli rather small, separated from the compound eye by more than their own minimum diameter; postclypeus moderately inflated, Pcl/W 0.29, Pcl/Ra 3.00–3.22, posterior margin evenly rounded, median suture distinct. Apical tooth of mandibles short, La/Li 0.52–0.56, Ra/Ri 0.75–0.83; accessory marginal tooth of the left mandible separated from the molar prominence in surface view by a distinct notch, compound ratio 7.70–9.10; tips of the apical and marginal teeth of the right mandible in the same line, the anterior edge of the first marginal tooth distinctly longer than that of the second. Pilosity of head capsule brown, uneven, not felted. Constriction between meso- and metanotum slightly wide, M/W 0.29–0.31. Third apical spur of fore tibia distinct.
